title: Clitoral erectile complex anatomy
description: A three-dimensional neurovascular and erectile complex: paired crura, body, glans and closely related vestibular bulbs.

questions.question: Is the clitoris only the visible glans?
questions.answer: No. The visible glans is part of a larger erectile complex that includes a body, paired crura and associated vestibular bulbs.

questions.question: Where are the clitoral crura located?
questions.answer: The crura extend along the ischiopubic rami beneath the vulvar surface and join the midline erectile body.

questions.question: What is the clitoral glans?
questions.answer: External distal part beneath or exposed by the hood; dense sensory innervation and distinct histology from cavernous bodies. Function: Conveys fine sensation.

questions.question: Where is the clitoral body located?
questions.answer: Midline body formed by apposition of the paired corpora cavernosa, deep to the external glans. Function: Engorges via cavernous vascular spaces.

questions.question: What is the function of the left corpus cavernosum?
questions.answer: Function: Contributes to body rigidity and expansion. Contralateral cavernous cylinder joining the body along the midline.
